target.title: fix(tui): suppress unhandled rejection from async agent event handler
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `onAgentEvent` callback in `EmbeddedTuiBackend` calls `void this.handleAgentEvent(evt)` without a `.catch()` handler. Since `handleAgentEvent` is async and can reject, this creates an unhandled promise rejection that crashes the TUI process.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add a noop `.catch(() => {})` to suppress the unhandled rejection, matching the pattern used elsewhere in the codebase for fire-and-forget async callbacks.

## User Impact

Prevents the TUI from crashing when an agent event handler throws.

## Evidence

### Behavior
The `onAgentEvent` callback now attaches a `.catch(() => {})` to the fire-and-forget `handleAgentEvent(evt)` promise.

### Source
`src/tui/embedded-backend.ts:325`
```ts
this.unsubscribe = onAgentEvent((evt) => {
  void this.handleAgentEvent(evt).catch(() => {});
});
```

### Test output
```
$ pnpm test -- src/tui/embedded-backend.test.ts --run
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.tui.config.ts
 ✓ |tui| src/tui/embedded-backend.test.ts (41 tests) 3511ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  41 passed (41)
   Duration  4.88s

[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 14.29s
```

### Notes
- This is a defensive fix; the callback is fire-and-forget by design.
- The `.catch(() => {})` pattern is already used elsewhere for similar fire-and-forget handlers.
- Existing tests continue to pass.
